ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: When the magnet starts moving above the center of the coil, if an induced current in the direction shown by the arrow in the figure is produced in the coil, in which direction does the magnet move?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a vertical bar magnet located above the center of a horizontal coil; the upper end of the magnet is marked as the S pole, and the lower end is marked as the N pole; the horizontal coil is drawn as an inclined planar quadrilateral, and on the front side of the coil near the observer, the arrow points to the right. From this arrow it can be judged that, viewed from top to bottom, the induced current in the coil goes around in the counterclockwise direction. Then reason: According to the right-hand rule, when the current is counterclockwise viewed from top to bottom, the direction of the induced magnetic field produced at the center of the coil is upward. The lower end of the magnet is the N pole, and the direction of the original magnetic field produced by the N pole at the coil below it is downward. Now the induced magnetic field is upward, indicating that it is opposing the increase of the downward magnetic flux. An increase in downward magnetic flux means that the N pole of the magnet is approaching the coil, so the magnet moves downward.
